'''Dawn Alisha Lott''' is an [[applied mathematician]] at [[Delaware State University]],{{r|about}} where she is a professor in the department of physical and computational sciences{{r|desfac}} and, since 2009, the director of the university's honors program.{{r|deshon}}

==Research==
Lott's research concerns [[numerical partial differential equations]] in [[solid mechanics]], [[fluid mechanics]], and [[biomechanics]].{{r|deshon|falconer}}
She has also published several papers on [[soliton]]s.{{r|about}}

==Education and career==
Lott is [[African-American]].{{r|bwm}}
She graduated from [[Bucknell University]] in 1987, with a bachelor's degree in mathematics, and earned a master's degree in mathematics from [[Michigan State University]] in 1989.{{r|about}} She did her doctoral work in Engineering Sciences and Applied Mathematics at [[Northwestern University]], completing her Ph.D. in 1994. Her dissertation, ''Adaptive Chebyshev Pseudo-Spectral Approximation for Shear Band Formation in Viscoplastic Materials'', was jointly supervised by Alvin Bayliss and [[Ted Belytschko]].{{r|about|mgp}}

After postdoctoral research from 1994 to 1997 at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], Lott became a faculty member at the [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]] in 1998.{{r|bwm}}
She moved to Delaware State in 2003.{{r|deshon}}In 2004, she was an [[EDGE Foundation|EDGE]] instructor.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=EDGE for Women|url=https://www.edgeforwomen.org/edge-2004/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906075141/http://www.edgeforwomen.org/edge-2004/ |archive-date=2015-09-06 |access-date=June 23, 2020|website=}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Lott was the [[AWM/MAA Falconer Lecturer]] for 2011. Her lecture concerned the mathematical treatment of [[aneurysm]]s.{{r|falconer}}

In 2013, Delaware State gave her their award for Faculty Excellence in Advising,{{r|desfea}} and in 2014 they gave her their award for Faculty Excellence in University and Community Service.{{r|desfeucs}}

Lott's accomplishments earned her recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2019 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Dawn A. Lott|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/dawn-a-lott/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612032827/https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/dawn-a-lott/ |archive-date=2020-06-12 |access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>

Lott was selected as a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the Class of 2021 "''for her deep commitment to the advancement of women as reflected through her many roles in AWM, the National Association of Mathematicians, and other associations as a committee member, leader, mentor, and speaker, and in supervision of several women obtaining the PhD or MS degree''".{{r|awmfellow}}
